full_judgment:
Muhammad Habibur Rahman, CJ: The plaintiff-respondents claimed ownership and possession of the suit land as successive heirs of the C.S. recorded tenants and even beyond. The suit was filed for a simple declaration of title owing to wrong recording of rights in the name of the defendants. 

 4. The trial court however discussed the oral and documentary evidence on record and found that the defendant could not file any sale certificate or other papers of the rent suit. The lower appellate court and the High Court Division found that the appellants could not file the relevant rent suit register and therefore the auction sale was not established. 

 5. The trial court however discussed the oral and documentary evidence on record and found that the plaintiff-respondents are not only not in possession of the suit land but that the appellants are in possession thereof for more than 40 years. The trial Court clearly held that the suit is not maintainable in this present form and is also barred by limitation.
